strengths.item: The paper is generally clear, well organized, and easy to inspect in standard ICLR format, with readable body text, consistent sectioning, and clean equation formatting across the main pages.
The mathematical notation and equations are mostly well typeset and cross-referenced clearly, even when some derivations are dense.
Captions for the main experimental tables and Figure 1 are informative and help explain datasets, metrics, averaging, and ablation settings.
Figure 1 and Table 3 on page 9 are legible and connected to nearby explanatory text, supporting verification of the noisy-setting, parameter-analysis, and ablation claims.

weaknesses.item: The main experimental tables on page 8 are visually dense, with many columns, small numeric text, multi-level headers, and numerous dividers, making comparisons harder to scan quickly.

Figure 1 is somewhat compact and visually busy, especially the parameter-analysis subplot with many numeric labels; some interpretation requires nearby prose rather than being fully clear from the figure alone.
Some abbreviations in compact tables, such as “Cls Conf” and “OOD Detect,” add minor reading friction.
The available inspection did not fully cover later appendix pages, so appendix table and figure legibility could not be completely verified.

dimension_review.evidence_summary: The PDF inspection found that pages 1–8 have a clean ICLR-style layout with readable text, standard headings, and generally clear equations. Page 8 contains Table 1 and Table 2, whose captions are helpful but whose dense formatting and small numerical entries make them relatively difficult to inspect. Page 9 contains Figure 1 and Table 3; both are legible and captioned, but Figure 1 and Table 3 are compact and require some effort to parse due to multiple curves, labels, grouped columns, abbreviations, and confidence statistics. References on pages 10–11 are conventionally formatted, with only minor extracted-text spacing artifacts.
dimension_review.rationale: The paper’s presentation is good overall: it is readable, organized, and mostly easy for reviewers to follow and verify. The main limitation is not conceptual disorganization but visual density in the experimental evidence, particularly large result tables and compact plots. These issues create minor-to-moderate inspection friction but do not make the paper hard to understand. Therefore, the appropriate ICLR Presentation score is 3 rather than 4.
